The first verse of the Qur’an is **Surah Al-Fatiha (1:1)** — the *Bismillah* (the opening invocation). In the standard Uthmani text, it is counted as verse 1.

**Exact Arabic text:**
> بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ

**Transliteration:**
> *Bismillāhi r-Raḥmāni r-Raḥīm*

**English translation** (e.g., Sahih International):
> **"In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."**

*(A common alternative rendering is: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.")*

**Note:** This verse opens every chapter of the Qur’an except Surah At-Tawbah (9). It is also recited at the beginning of nearly every Surah and is considered the first verse of the Qur’an in the standard numbering system used worldwide.

**Surah Al-Ikhlas (112), Verse 1**

**Arabic text:**
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Say, 'He is Allah, [who is] One'"

*(Context: This is the opening verse of Surah Al-Ikhlas, the chapter of sincere devotion, which affirms the absolute oneness of God.)*

The first verse of Surah **Ya-Sin** (Chapter 36) is:

**Arabic text:**
> **يس**

**Transliteration:** *Yā Sīn*

**English translation (e.g., Sahih International):**
> **"Ya, Sin."**

*(Or simply: **"Ya Sin."**)*

**Context:** This is one of the *Muqatta'at* (disjointed letters) that open several chapters of the Qur'an. The meaning of these letters is known to God alone, though the surah itself is named after them—**Surah Ya-Sin**. The very next verse (36:2) begins: *"By the wise Qur'an..."* (*Wa al-Qur'ani al-Hakim*).

**Surah Al-Hujurat (49), Verse 12**

**Arabic text:**
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا ۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَّحِيمٌ

**English translation (approximate):**
"O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful."

This is **Surah An-Nur (24:35)**, the famous **Ayat al-Nur** (Verse of Light).

**Exact Arabic text (Uthmani script with tashkeel):**

اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ الزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ لِنُورِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

**English translation** (Sahih International):

> Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star. It is lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if it had not been touched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.

*(Note: Slight variations exist among translations—e.g., “niche” vs. “lamp-niche,” “pearly star” vs. “shining star”—but the meaning is consistent across standard renderings.)*

**Surah Al-ʿAṣr (103), verse 2**

**Arabic text:**
إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Indeed, mankind is in loss."

*(Context: The full chapter reads: "By time, indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.")*

**Surah Luqman (31), Verse 13**

**Arabic text:**
وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ

**Transliteration:**
Wa-idh qāla Luqmānu li-ibnihi wa-huwa yaʿiẓuhu yā bunayya lā tushrik bil-lāhi inna ash-shirka laẓulmun ʿaẓīm

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"And [remember] when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, 'O my son, do not associate others with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice.'"

*(Note: The preceding verse, 31:12, mentions that God gave Luqman wisdom and told him to be grateful; verse 13 then records Luqman’s advice to his son.)*

**Arabic text (Surah Al-Mujadila, 58:11):**

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ

**English translation (approximate):**

*O you who have believed, when it is said to you, “Make room in the assemblies,” then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when it is said, “Rise up,” then rise up; Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.*

*(Note: The word “unshūzū” / “rise up” is paired with “yarfa‘” / “He will raise” — a wordplay in the original Arabic: when you rise up (to make room or leave), Allah raises you in rank.)*

**Surah Al-Ankabut (29), Verse 45**

**Arabic text:**
اتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ ۚ إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنكَرِ ۗ وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ

**Surah Al-Mutaffifin (83), Verse 1**

**Arabic text:**
وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ

**Transliteration:**
*Waylun lil-muṭaffifīn*

**English translation (Sahih International):**
"Woe to the defrauders,"

**Translation (Yusuf Ali / general):**
"Woe to those who give short measure!"

This verse opens Surah 83, which condemns those who cheat in weights and measures (specifically giving less than is due to others). The word *muṭaffifīn* (مُطَفِّفِينَ) refers to those who deal fraudulently, particularly in commercial transactions.

**Surah Al-Ahqaf (46), verse 9**

**Arabic text (Uthmani script):**
> قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدِيعًا مِّنَ الرُّسُلِ وَلَا أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلَا لَكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ ۚ وَمَا أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ

**English translation (approximate meaning):**
> Say, “I am not unprecedented among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.”

*(A common rendering: “Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.’”)*
